newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TNT says higher 1st half profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TNT says higher 1st half profit.

text.p: Transport group TNT Ltd said on Wednesday it expected its first half profit for the current 1996/97 year to be better than a year ago.
"Yes, we certainly would expect the first half to be better than last year," TNT chief executive David Mortimer told reporters after the annual meeting.
TNT is currently under an agreed A$2.0 billion takeover bid from Dutch postal and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland Nv (KPN).
"A big factor in the TNT results last year was Ansett. It is no longer of the operation, so the decoupling of those equity accounted losses has a significant positive effect," Mortimer said.
The company earlier told shareholders that first quarter oeprating profit had risen 14.7 percent to A$27.0 million, while net profit had more than doubled to A$27.87 million.
Both Mortimer and TNT Chairman Fred Millar said they expected the KPN bid to succeed, citing the lack of any rival bid and likely regulatory approval in Europe and Australia.
TNT reported an equity accounted net profit of A$46.69 million for the six months to December 31, 1995 from A$73.10 million the previous year.
TNT sold its 50 percent stake in Ansett Australia to Air New Zealand in September.
